subject: math.HO
name: Pythagorean theorem
statement: In a Euclidean right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse length equals the sum of the squares of the other two side lengths.

subject: math.HO
name: Euclid’s theorem on primes
statement: There are infinitely many prime numbers.

subject: math.HO
name: Euclidean algorithm theorem
statement: Repeatedly replacing a pair of positive integers (a,b), with a ≥ b, by (b,a mod b), stopping when the second entry becomes zero, terminates. The last nonzero entry is the greatest common divisor of the original integers.

subject: math.HO
name: Archimedes’ quadrature of the parabola
statement: The area of a parabolic segment bounded by a chord and a parabola is four-thirds the area of the inscribed triangle whose base is the chord and whose third vertex has a tangent parallel to that chord.

subject: math.HO
name: Newton’s generalized binomial theorem
statement: For a complex number α and |z|<1, (1+z)^α = Σ from k=0 to infinity of binom(α,k)zᵏ, where binom(α,k)=α(α−1)⋯(α−k+1)/k! and binom(α,0)=1. The power is defined using the analytic logarithm of 1+z that is zero at z=0.

subject: math.HO
name: Euler’s Basel theorem
statement: The sum of the reciprocals of the squares of the positive integers is π²/6: Σ from n=1 to infinity of 1/n²=π²/6.

subject: math.HO
name: Euler’s formula for complex exponentials
statement: For every real number x, e^(ix)=cos(x)+i sin(x), where i²=−1. In particular, e^(iπ)+1=0.

subject: math.HO
name: Euler’s theorem on trails
statement: A finite undirected graph with at least one edge has a trail traversing each edge exactly once if and only if all its non-isolated vertices belong to one connected component and it has either zero or two vertices of odd degree. Such a trail is closed if and only if every vertex has even degree.

subject: math.HO
name: Lagrange’s four-square theorem
statement: Every nonnegative integer is a sum of four squares of integers, allowing zero squares.

subject: math.HO
name: Fundamental theorem of algebra
statement: Every polynomial of positive degree with complex coefficients has a complex root, and hence factors completely into linear factors over the complex numbers.

subject: math.HO
name: Abel–Ruffini theorem
statement: There is no formula using finitely many arithmetic operations and extraction of radicals that solves the general polynomial equation of degree five or higher from its coefficients. Some particular equations of these degrees are nevertheless solvable by radicals.

subject: math.HO
name: Galois’ solvability theorem
statement: A polynomial over a field of characteristic zero is solvable by radicals if and only if the Galois group of its splitting field over that field is a solvable group.

subject: math.HO
name: Cantor’s uncountability theorem
statement: There is no bijection between the positive integers and the real numbers; already the real interval [0,1] is uncountable.

subject: math.HO
name: Jordan curve theorem
statement: Every simple closed curve in the plane separates the plane into exactly two connected components, one bounded and one unbounded, and the curve is the boundary of both components.

subject: math.HO
name: Gödel’s first incompleteness theorem
statement: Every consistent, computably axiomatized first-order theory that contains Robinson arithmetic has a sentence that the theory can neither prove nor refute. Here refuting a sentence means proving its negation.

subject: math.HO
name: Undecidability of the halting problem
statement: No algorithm can correctly determine, for every program and every input, whether that program eventually halts on that input.

subject: math.HO
name: Fermat’s last theorem
statement: For every integer n>2, there are no positive integers a,b,c satisfying aⁿ+bⁿ=cⁿ.

subject: math.HO
name: Four-color theorem
statement: Every finite planar graph without loops admits a vertex coloring with at most four colors in which the endpoints of every edge have different colors.

subject: math.HO
name: Feuerbach’s theorem
statement: For every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle, its nine-point circle is tangent internally to its incircle and externally to each of its three excircles, with coincidence of the incircle and nine-point circle in the equilateral case.

subject: math.HO
name: Morley’s trisector theorem
statement: In any nondegenerate Euclidean triangle, the three intersections of adjacent internal angle trisectors, one near each side, form an equilateral triangle.
